case.decision_point: During elective open hernia surgery after two separate cord-like structures are seen, before postoperative ultrasound or follow-up.

case.initial_facts:
A man in his 60s has a year of intermittent right-groin discomfort with exertion or standing and a reducible inguinal hernia. He has no previous inguinal operation, trauma, urinary symptoms or testicular pain. The scrotal examination was normal. No preoperative imaging was obtained for the uncomplicated clinical hernia.
During elective open repair, two distinct spermatic-cord structures are unexpectedly identified. Each appears to contain a vas and vascular/neural elements; both are traced towards the testis and through a common internal ring. Later ultrasound and postoperative outcome are not available at this decision point. No assumption should be made that an asymptomatic anatomical variant had to be predicted before the operation.

requirements.requirement: Clarify the course and components of both structures before division.
requirements.presentation_based_rationale: A mistaken anatomical assumption could cause harm.
requirements.acceptable_requests_or_alternatives: Careful operative identification with specialist help as needed.
requirements.deadline: Before the indicated clinical decision in a future interactive task; not elicited or scored in this written batch.

case.reference: Distinguish apparent duplicated cord/vas anatomy from other surgical structures and preserve both vascular/ductal pathways while seeking appropriate specialist judgement. Avoid cutting or sacrificing an unidentified structure merely to fit usual anatomy. Document the finding and the limits of visual confirmation; do not infer a postoperative perfusion result. Preoperative non-detection of an unexpected variant is not itself an information-seeking failure in an uncomplicated hernia. Original ultrasound images were not exportable later; that is a record limitation, not a negative study.
case.hidden: Modified repair, postoperative ultrasound report with preserved arterial flow and short follow-up.
review_questions: Which intraoperative verification and preservation actions are essential?
How much anatomical certainty is justified from the supplied operative observations?
